text:
jordan_support: Heads-up from customer AuroraData (ticket #8202). They're processing streaming completions + fncall events into an event store and need resume semantics when client connections drop. Right now they lose partial structured outputs and there's no way to reconcile on reconnect. Blocking their integration.

lena_sales: Aurora is on Dedicated-us-east and this is blocking their pilot. They asked if we can expose stable per-frame sequence numbers + an optional resume token in streams so their parser can request missing frames on reconnect.

omar_product: Can you paste an anonymized capture and a short description of what they expect? Also do they need server-side retention of buffered frames or just client-supplied checkpoints?

jordan_support: Their capture: ```
[chunk A] {"seq":null,"type":"delta","text":"Payment intent created..."}
[chunk B] {"seq":null,"type":"tool_event","name":"confirm_payment","payload":"{\"id\":\"pay_789\",\"status\":\"ok\"}"}
// connection dropped after chunk B. On reconnect, they get a new stream with no seq info so they can't tell where to resume. They want to avoid double-processing and reparse costs.
```

cleo_eng: We currently do not attach stable per-frame seq ids to streaming frames; internal IDs exist but are not part of the public contract. Implementing a resume API requires defining retention window, ids, and replay endpoints or at least stable event ids clients can use for idempotent dedupe.

omar_product: Product options: 
1) Add lightweight per-frame headers: X-RW-Seq: integer and X-RW-Resume-Token: opaque string. No server replay; clients use tokens to ask upstream for missing events from their server logs (best-effort). Low effort.
2) Server-side short-term replay: server retains last N seconds/frames per session and exposes a small replay endpoint to fetch missing frames by seq range or resume token. Medium effort and infra impact.
3) Higher-level SDK helpers + docs: provide client-side checkpoint helper + examples for idempotent webhook handlers (docs only). Low effort but requires customer work.

lena_sales: Aurora prefers 2 ideally but will accept 1 if quicker — they want explicit sequence numbers so their consumer can at least de-dupe and resume by asking us for missing ranges later.

tara_pm: We need a decision today to scope a hotfix vs roadmap item. If we do 1 (headers only) as short-term, define launch criteria and estimate eng effort.

cleo_eng: Estimates: option 1 (headers + stable ids in-stream) = ~2 dev-days + 0.5 QA + docs. Option 2 (short replay buffer + replay API) = ~6-10 dev-days + infra changes + retention SLOs. Option 3 (docs/SDK) = 1 dev-day + docs + examples.

omar_product: Proposed acceptance for Option 1 (short-term):
- frames include stable seq and resume token header documented in API spec
- unit tests showing reconnect and client de-dupe patterns
- e2e with Aurora on staging demonstrating they can de-dupe and reconcile after disconnect
- rollout gated behind a feature flag for Dedicated customers initially
- customer-facing docs snippet and SDK helper in JS/Go

deploy-bot: maintenance-window-check: us-east tonight 01:30 EDT -> available

jordan_support: Aurora engineer can test staging at 23:00 EDT tonight if we provide endpoint+flag name.

lena_sales: We'll push for Option 1 now to unblock them; plan Option 2 for Q2 as dedicated replay for high-reliability customers.

omar_product: Decision: proceed with Option 1 as an API-level compatibility improvement (headers + stable ids + SDK helper). Schedule Option 2 for roadmap refinement next quarter. @cleo_eng can you take a ticket?

cleo_eng: Creating GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/10333 title: "feat(streaming): expose per-frame seq + resume-token (opt-in)". Assigning to mike_eng. ETA: start tonight, staging tomorrow.

mike_eng: Taking it. Plan: add X-RW-Seq and X-RW-Resume headers on streaming frames and include the fields in event payloads for consumers that want them. Add JS helper that writes checkpoint to durable store and resumes by providing last seq on reconnect. Will add unit + integration tests and small docs PR.

tara_pm: I'll own rollout checklist and acceptance criteria. Once Aurora validates staging we do 5% canary for 4 hours, monitor for backward compatibility issues. Rollback by disabling the feature flag for Dedicated.

jordan_support: Updating ticket #8202 and will coordinate Aurora's staging test.

lena_sales: Thanks team. Also prepare a short FAQ for customers explaining semantics: "headers are opt-in; they are best-effort sequence numbers with retention window; not a guaranteed long-term message queue."

omar_product: Good call, include retention window and expected replay semantics. We'll treat replay as a separate product project.

mike_eng: Starting work. Will post PR + staging URL when ready.
